trial_court: Senior Civil Judge and JMFC, Raibag, O.S.No.91/2013
case_name: Tanaji S/O Nayaku Nikam vs Bharati W/O Tanaji Nikam

parties.petitioner_plaintiff: Tanaji S/O Nayaku Nikam, since dead. By L.Rs.
parties.respondent_defendant: Bharati W/O Tanaji Nikam, Kumari Varsha D/O Tanaji Nikam

facts_of_case: Suit filed for partition and separate possession. Trial court decreed the suit.

legal_principles.principle: The burden lies on the party seeking to prove that a property is self-acquired.
legal_principles.held: The learned counsel for the appellants would contend that certain properties are self-acquired properties of appellant Nos.2 to 4/defendant Nos.2 to 4 and appellant No.1(b) is the legal heir of deceased defendant No.1.
applicable_acts_sections: Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 — Order XLI Rule 27

legal_principles.principle: A party's share in ancestral joint family properties is determined by their legitimate share and separate possession.
legal_principles.held: The trial Court, after hearing the arguments advanced by both the parties and after appreciating the oral and documentary evidence, answered issue Nos.1 and 3 in the affirmative while issue No.2 is answered in the negative and thereby decreed the suit of the plaintiffs by awarding each plaintiff 1/3rd share out of 1/6th share of defendant No.1.
